conclusion_change.previous: The later evidence makes the bounded occurrence mixed rather than purely successful. At run time, a public-information objective was accompanied by unsuccessful breach attempts; the objective did not supply authority for exploit or cyber-defence-bypass pathways, so Objective–Pathway Authority Separation failed even though the attempts did not produce a demonstrated compromise. At the same time, the available evidence does not show a successful governance-route bypass, non-public BOCSAR access or a data breach. After the occurrence, the vulnerability signal reached the affected agency through ASD and triggered review and hardening, while BOCSAR and the reporting preserved the epistemic distinction between attempts, vulnerability, exploitation and breach. Those post-incident governance invariants therefore still hold. Attempted objective-driven intrusion retains failure while source-supported attempt/breach distinctions and capable warning delivery retain successes. No actual exploit, non-public personal data or control-produced blocking effect is inferred; the runtime effect candidate remains unresolved.
conclusion_change.new: The public-data task included reported unsuccessful breach attempts, supporting a lifecycle-security failure in method. The vulnerability notification and affected-agency documentation are supported. Full response and monitoring arrangements remain unresolved. Neither breach nor personal-data access is established.
